$comment: Exceptions for host-quarantine-headers.test.ts. hostSafe: suites the rules flag that are safe on the owner's machine by design. headerRequired: suites the rules cannot see that stay off the host anyway, most of them because they reach icacls, a real CLI or reg.exe through app code (each reason says what a run on the test VM recorded). Every entry needs a reason. A path may use * for part of one path segment, and must then match exactly one file.

hostSafe.reason: Names icacls only in its fake child_process, whose execFile and execFileSync answer the only program starts the code it drives makes (the account store's rights tool and the owner-only rule); the network is faked and the account folders are its own temp ones. No process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.

Names icacls only in its fake child_process, which answers or refuses every program start the code it drives makes (the agent's own start is a recorded fake); the owner-only rule is a test rule and the shared-folder links are stubbed. No process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.

Names icacls only in its fake child_process, which answers or refuses every program start the code it drives makes; the terminal and the headless runs are fakes, the owner-only rule is a test rule and the shared-folder links are stubbed. No process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.

Names icacls only as a program its fake execFile answers from an in-memory record of each folder's owner and rights; every other child_process call refuses. Real temp folders are made, but no process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.

Names icacls only in its in-memory Windows (the programs, the file system and PowerShell are all fakes) and in prose; every child_process call refuses. No process starts and no real folder is touched.

Names icacls only in its fake child_process, which answers or refuses every program start the code it drives makes; the headless runner is a recording fake, the owner-only rule is a test rule and the account resolver links nothing. No process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.
Reads and parses source files only: the process calls the rules see are text inside its self-test strings, never run. No process starts.
Runs read-only git (ls-files, check-attr) against this checkout; changes nothing.

Names icacls only inside the Feature Guide words it pins (what to let run when the sign-in folder check gets no answer); it only reads the app's text, its documents and recorded fixtures. No process starts, no ACL is changed and no link is made.

Tests the home guard itself and must run on the host; every real-home link, write and spawn target it names is built to fail harmlessly (a source that does not exist, a folder that does not exist, node -e 0).
The WP1 legacy-name gate: runs read-only git (cat-file, ls-tree) against this checkout. Named by pattern so this list adds no line to the WP1 legacy-name manifest.
Runs read-only git (merge-base, rev-parse, diff) against this checkout; the cases that would fetch are given a fake git.
